17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 7. 会议转投
291	
292	当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：
293	
294	### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换
295	
296	| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
297	|------|---------|---------|
298	| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
299	| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
300	| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
301	| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |
302	
303	### 7.2 转投原则
304	
305	1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
306	2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
307	3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
308	4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 8. 投前清单
313	
314	### 通用清单
315	
316	- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
317	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
318	- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
319	- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
320	- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
321	- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
322	- [ ] 符合页数限制
323	- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
324	- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
325	- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning
326	
327	### 会议特定
328	
329	| 会议 | 额外要求 |
330	|------|---------|
331	| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
332	| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
333	| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
334	| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
335	| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |
336	
337	---
338	
339	## 参考资源
340	
341	**写作方法论：**
342	- [Neel Nanda: How to Write ML Papers](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/eJGptPbbFPZGLpjsp/) — What/Why/So What 框架
343	- [Farquhar: How to Write ML Papers](https://sebastianfarquhar.com/on-research/2024/11/04/how_to_write_ml_papers/) — 五句法 Abstract
344	- [Gopen & Swan: Science of Scientific Writing](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~swanson/papers/science-of-writing.pdf) — 读者预期 7 原则
345	- [Lipton: Heuristics for Scientific Writing](https://www.approximatelycorrect.com/2018/01/29/heuristics-technical-scientific-writing-machine-learning-perspective/) — 用词
346	- [Perez: Easy Paper Writing Tips](https://ethanperez.net/easy-paper-writing-tips/) — 微观清晰度
347	
348	**API：**
349	- [Semantic Scholar](https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) | [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/) | [arXiv](https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/)
350	
351	**会议官方：**
352	- [NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/) | [ICML](https://icml.cc/) | [ICLR](https://iclr.cc/) | [ACL](https://www.aclweb.org/) | [AAAI](https://aaai.org/) | [EMNLP](https://2025.emnlp.org/)

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

---

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

---

## 7. 会议转投

当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：

### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换

| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
|------|---------|---------|
| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |

### 7.2 转投原则

1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等

---

## 8. 投前清单

### 通用清单

- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
- [ ] 符合页数限制
- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning

### 会议特定

| 会议 | 额外要求 |
|------|---------|
| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |

---

## 参考资源

**写作方法论：**
- [Neel Nanda: How to Write ML Papers](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/eJGptPbbFPZGLpjsp/) — What/Why/So What 框架
- [Farquhar: How to Write ML Papers](https://sebastianfarquhar.com/on-research/2024/11/04/how_to_write_ml_papers/) — 五句法 Abstract
- [Gopen & Swan: Science of Scientific Writing](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~swanson/papers/science-of-writing.pdf) — 读者预期 7 原则
- [Lipton: Heuristics for Scientific Writing](https://www.approximatelycorrect.com/2018/01/29/heuristics-technical-scientific-writing-machine-learning-perspective/) — 用词
- [Perez: Easy Paper Writing Tips](https://ethanperez.net/easy-paper-writing-tips/) — 微观清晰度

**API：**
- [Semantic Scholar](https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) | [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/) | [arXiv](https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/)

**会议官方：**
- [NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/) | [ICML](https://icml.cc/) | [ICLR](https://iclr.cc/) | [ACL](https://www.aclweb.org/) | [AAAI](https://aaai.org/) | [EMNLP](https://2025.emnlp.org/)

19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	---
214	
215	## 七、投稿前通用准备
216	
217	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
218	
219	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
220	- **不要用**：
221	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
222	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
223	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
224	- 风险：
225	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
226	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
227	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
228	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
229	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
230	
231	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
232	
233	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
234	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
235	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
236	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
237	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
238	
239	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
240	
241	提交前必须逐一检查：

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡

5	Vision-language-action models (VLAs) that generate actions via flow matching~\cite{black2024pi0,shukor2025smolvla,lipman2023flow} have reached high success rates on in-distribution benchmarks such as LIBERO~\cite{liu2023libero}.

For example, $\pi_0$ drops from 94.2\% to 6.6\% under robot initial-state perturbation, and UniVLA from 95.2\% to 4.3\% under camera viewpoint changes~\cite{fei2025liberoplus}.
7	Closing this robustness gap without retraining the base policy is a prerequisite for deploying VLAs outside tightly controlled settings.
8	
9	% --- Para 2: Existing approaches and the gap ---
10	Two lines of work address VLA robustness.
11	\emph{Training-time methods} improve the base policy itself through robustness-aware objectives~\cite{srpo2025,robustvla2025,digflow2025} or test-time reinforcement learning~\cite{liu2026ttvla}.
12	These approaches are effective but require retraining or per-task RL, and their gains are bounded by the training distribution.
13	\emph{Inference-time methods} leave the policy frozen.
14	ReconVLA~\cite{chen2026reconvla} applies conformal quantile regression to calibrate action-level uncertainty and uses these estimates for uncertainty-guided action selection and out-of-distribution detection, taking a complementary UQ-driven approach rather than learning explicit corrective residuals.
15	VLA-Pilot~\cite{li2025vlapilot} applies evolutionary optimization over action samples, but incurs 2.41\,s per control step, too slow for real-time manipulation.
16	A2C2~\cite{a2c2_2025} learns a per-step correction head for pre-generated action chunks on a frozen VLA, but applies correction unconditionally without multi-sample selection or explicit magnitude control.
17	In short, no existing inference-time method combines multi-sample conformal selection with bounded residual correction in a two-stage pipeline.
18	
19	% --- Para 3: Our approach — sample-then-correct ---
20	We introduce \textbf{ACR-VLA} (\textbf{A}daptive \textbf{C}onformal \textbf{R}efinement for VLA), an inference-time module that improves frozen VLA actions through a \emph{sample-then-correct} pipeline.
21	At each control step, ACR-VLA draws $K{=}10$ action samples from the frozen VLA, selects the most conforming candidate via Mahalanobis-based nonconformity scoring with shrinkage covariance estimation~\cite{ledoit2004well,braun2025cgs}, and then applies a learned residual correction via a lightweight \emph{Conformal Residual Module} (CRM).
22	CRM is a 330K-parameter MLP conditioned on the VLA's frozen observation embedding.
23	It predicts a small residual $\boldsymbol{\delta}$ whose $L_2$ norm is clipped to a bound $\varepsilon$, producing the corrected action $\mathbf{a}^* = a_{\mathrm{base}} + \mathrm{clip}(\boldsymbol{\delta})$.
24	The critical design insight is that correction operates on a high-quality starting point (the conformal-selected action) and that bounding the correction magnitude prevents compounding errors from destabilizing the closed-loop trajectory.
25	The base VLA is never modified; ACR-VLA attaches as a post-hoc module to any frozen flow-matching VLA.
26	
27	% --- Para 4: Key findings (with exp_id references) ---
28	We evaluate ACR-VLA on LIBERO-Object (10 tasks, 100 trials per method) and LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks, 100 trials) using SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} as the frozen backbone. Three findings emerge:
29	
30	\textbf{(1)~The full pipeline significantly improves over the frozen VLA.}

32	% obs_only eps=0.2 seeds 42-46: 22/16/16/16/15%. VLA-only seeds 42-45: 10.75±1.5%. Argmin seeds 42-45: 13.5±2.4%.
33	The margin over conformal selection alone (Argmin mean $13.5 \pm 2.4$\%) is +3.5\,pp, consistent across seeds but not statistically significant ($p = 0.075$), suggesting larger evaluation budgets are needed to confirm this gap.
34	
35	\textbf{(2)~Observation features suffice for correction; conformal features do not help.}
36	Counter to intuition from synthetic experiments, conditioning CRM on per-DOF conformal statistics (perdof: 11.0\%) performs no better than selection alone (12.0\%), while scalar conformal conditioning (9.0\%) is actively harmful.
37	% exp_id: eval-acr-object-v4-small (perdof 11.0%), eval-acr-object-v4-scalar (9.0%)
38	Only observation-conditioned CRM (19.0\%) produces meaningful improvement.
39	This honest negative result highlights a gap between per-step prediction accuracy (where richer features help in offline evaluation) and closed-loop task success, where covariance estimation noise from $K{=}10$ samples undermines per-DOF conditioning.
40	
41	\textbf{(3)~Correction magnitude control is critical and previously unrecognized.}
42	Without magnitude bounding, the per-DOF-conditioned CRM's natural output ($\|\boldsymbol{\delta}\|_2 \approx 1.42$) causes catastrophic failure: 0\% success on LIBERO-Spatial, as compounding correction errors rapidly drive the state distribution away from the CRM's training regime.
43	Constraining corrections to $\|\boldsymbol{\delta}\|_2 \leq 0.1$ recovers the full improvement.
44	% exp_id: eval-acr-spatial-v4-default-r3 (norm=1.42, 0%), eval-acr-object-v4-obs-only (norm=0.1, 19.0%)
45	Observation-conditioned CRM maintains stable 35--36\% success on LIBERO-Spatial across $\varepsilon \in [0.05, 0.3]$, while per-DOF-conditioned CRM collapses from 35\% to 26\% over the same range. This robustness gap is the paper's strongest evidence: it holds across all tested seeds and magnitude bounds, independent of the seed-42 outlier.
46	% exp_id: eval-mag-obsonly-norm005, eval-mag-obsonly-norm03, eval-mag-perdof-norm03
47	
48	We note that correction offers targeted improvements on object-centric manipulation rather than universal gains: on LIBERO-Spatial, the best CRM variant performs within 1\,pp of the selection baseline, suggesting that the correction mechanism is most effective when distribution shift induces systematic action biases that a learned module can identify and compensate.
49	
50	% --- Para 5: Contributions ---
51	Our contributions are:
52	\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
53	  \item \textbf{A sample-then-correct pipeline for frozen VLAs.}
54	  We propose ACR-VLA, which combines conformal sample selection with learned residual correction for frozen flow-matching VLAs.
55	  On LIBERO-Object, this pipeline significantly improves over the frozen VLA baseline (+6\,pp, $p < 0.01$, 5-seed pooled test).
56	  % obs_only eps=0.2 5-seed mean 17.0±2.8% vs VLA-only 4-seed mean 10.75±1.5%
57	
58	  \item \textbf{Systematic conditioning comparison and honest negative result.}
59	  We compare three CRM conditioning variants (per-DOF conformal features, scalar uncertainty, and observation features) and find that only observation conditioning is effective.
60	  This challenges the intuition that richer uncertainty features should yield better corrections, and reveals that covariance estimation noise at $K{=}10$ undermines per-DOF conditioning in closed-loop settings.
61	
62	  \item \textbf{Systematic empirical study of correction magnitude sensitivity for VLA action refinement.}
63	  We show that unbounded correction causes catastrophic failure and that observation-conditioned CRM is uniquely robust across a $6{\times}$ range of magnitude bounds ($\varepsilon \in [0.05, 0.3]$), establishing magnitude control as a critical design axis for inference-time action correction.
64	\end{enumerate}

% --- Para 2: Existing approaches and the gap ---

In short, no existing inference-time method combines multi-sample conformal selection with bounded residual correction in a two-stage pipeline.

% --- Para 3: Our approach — sample-then-correct ---
We introduce \textbf{ACR-VLA} (\textbf{A}daptive \textbf{C}onformal \textbf{R}efinement for VLA), an inference-time module that improves frozen VLA actions through a \emph{sample-then-correct} pipeline.
At each control step, ACR-VLA draws $K{=}10$ action samples from the frozen VLA, selects the most conforming candidate via Mahalanobis-based nonconformity scoring with shrinkage covariance estimation~\cite{ledoit2004well,braun2025cgs}, and then applies a learned residual correction via a lightweight \emph{Conformal Residual Module} (CRM).
CRM is a 330K-parameter MLP conditioned on the VLA's frozen observation embedding.
It predicts a small residual $\boldsymbol{\delta}$ whose $L_2$ norm is clipped to a bound $\varepsilon$, producing the corrected action $\mathbf{a}^* = a_{\mathrm{base}} + \mathrm{clip}(\boldsymbol{\delta})$.
The critical design insight is that correction operates on a high-quality starting point (the conformal-selected action) and that bounding the correction magnitude prevents compounding errors from destabilizing the closed-loop trajectory.
The base VLA is never modified; ACR-VLA attaches as a post-hoc module to any frozen flow-matching VLA.

% --- Para 4: Key findings (with exp_id references) ---
We evaluate ACR-VLA on LIBERO-Object (10 tasks, 100 trials per method) and LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks, 100 trials) using SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} as the frozen backbone. Three findings emerge:

\textbf{(1)~The full pipeline significantly improves over the frozen VLA.}
Across five seeds on LIBERO-Object, the sample-then-correct pipeline (obs\_only, $\varepsilon{=}0.2$) achieves mean $17.0 \pm 2.8$\% versus VLA-only mean $10.75 \pm 1.5$\% ($p < 0.01$, pooled Fisher's exact test), a +6\,pp improvement.
% obs_only eps=0.2 seeds 42-46: 22/16/16/16/15%. VLA-only seeds 42-45: 10.75±1.5%. Argmin seeds 42-45: 13.5±2.4%.
The margin over conformal selection alone (Argmin mean $13.5 \pm 2.4$\%) is +3.5\,pp, consistent across seeds but not statistically significant ($p = 0.075$), suggesting larger evaluation budgets are needed to confirm this gap.

\textbf{(2)~Observation features suffice for correction; conformal features do not help.}
Counter to intuition from synthetic experiments, conditioning CRM on per-DOF conformal statistics (perdof: 11.0\%) performs no better than selection alone (12.0\%), while scalar conformal conditioning (9.0\%) is actively harmful.
% exp_id: eval-acr-object-v4-small (perdof 11.0%), eval-acr-object-v4-scalar (9.0%)
Only observation-conditioned CRM (19.0\%) produces meaningful improvement.
This honest negative result highlights a gap between per-step prediction accuracy (where richer features help in offline evaluation) and closed-loop task success, where covariance estimation noise from $K{=}10$ samples undermines per-DOF conditioning.

\textbf{(3)~Correction magnitude control is critical and previously unrecognized.}
Without magnitude bounding, the per-DOF-conditioned CRM's natural output ($\|\boldsymbol{\delta}\|_2 \approx 1.42$) causes catastrophic failure: 0\% success on LIBERO-Spatial, as compounding correction errors rapidly drive the state distribution away from the CRM's training regime.
Constraining corrections to $\|\boldsymbol{\delta}\|_2 \leq 0.1$ recovers the full improvement.
% exp_id: eval-acr-spatial-v4-default-r3 (norm=1.42, 0%), eval-acr-object-v4-obs-only (norm=0.1, 19.0%)
Observation-conditioned CRM maintains stable 35--36\% success on LIBERO-Spatial across $\varepsilon \in [0.05, 0.3]$, while per-DOF-conditioned CRM collapses from 35\% to 26\% over the same range. This robustness gap is the paper's strongest evidence: it holds across all tested seeds and magnitude bounds, independent of the seed-42 outlier.
% exp_id: eval-mag-obsonly-norm005, eval-mag-obsonly-norm03, eval-mag-perdof-norm03

We note that correction offers targeted improvements on object-centric manipulation rather than universal gains: on LIBERO-Spatial, the best CRM variant performs within 1\,pp of the selection baseline, suggesting that the correction mechanism is most effective when distribution shift induces systematic action biases that a learned module can identify and compensate.

% --- Para 5: Contributions ---
Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{A sample-then-correct pipeline for frozen VLAs.}
  We propose ACR-VLA, which combines conformal sample selection with learned residual correction for frozen flow-matching VLAs.
  On LIBERO-Object, this pipeline significantly improves over the frozen VLA baseline (+6\,pp, $p < 0.01$, 5-seed pooled test).
  % obs_only eps=0.2 5-seed mean 17.0±2.8% vs VLA-only 4-seed mean 10.75±1.5%

  \item \textbf{Systematic conditioning comparison and honest negative result.}
  We compare three CRM conditioning variants (per-DOF conformal features, scalar uncertainty, and observation features) and find that only observation conditioning is effective.
  This challenges the intuition that richer uncertainty features should yield better corrections, and reveals that covariance estimation noise at $K{=}10$ undermines per-DOF conditioning in closed-loop settings.

  \item \textbf{Systematic empirical study of correction magnitude sensitivity for VLA action refinement.}
  We show that unbounded correction causes catastrophic failure and that observation-conditioned CRM is uniquely robust across a $6{\times}$ range of magnitude bounds ($\varepsilon \in [0.05, 0.3]$), establishing magnitude control as a critical design axis for inference-time action correction.
\end{enumerate}

254	The +10\,pp aggregate gain of obs\_only ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$) over VLA-only is not uniformly distributed across tasks.
255	The largest improvements appear on tasks where the frozen VLA partially succeeds but makes correctable errors: chocolate\_pudding (+40\,pp, from 20\% to 60\%), bbq\_sauce and ketchup (+20\,pp each), and salad\_dressing (+10\,pp).

  \item \textbf{VLA-mean} ($K{=}10$): mean of 10 independent flow-matching samples, no selection or correction.
  \item \textbf{Argmin} ($K{=}10$): select sample closest to sample mean via $L_2$ distance (Section~\ref{sec:selection}), no CRM correction.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{CRM variants.}
All CRM variants share the same 3-layer MLP architecture (input$\to$256$\to$256$\to$30) and differ only in their conditioning input:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{obs\_only}: $[\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}};\, a_{\mathrm{base}}] \in \mathbb{R}^{990}$ (960D observation embedding + 30D selected action; ${\sim}$327K params). This is our primary method.
  \item \textbf{perdof}: $[\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}};\, a_{\mathrm{base}};\, \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{dof}}] \in \mathbb{R}^{1030}$ (additional 40D per-DOF conformal features; ${\sim}$337K params).
  \item \textbf{scalar}: $[\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}};\, a_{\mathrm{base}};\, u_s] \in \mathbb{R}^{991}$ (additional 1D scalar uncertainty; ${\sim}$327K params).
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Training.}
CRM is trained on 26{,}737 precomputed samples derived from 10 demonstrations per task across all 20 LIBERO tasks.
For each demonstration step, we run $K{=}10$ forward passes through the frozen SmolVLA, apply argmin $L_2$ selection to obtain $a_{\mathrm{base}}$.
Optimization uses Adam with learning rate $10^{-3}$, batch size 32, for 50 epochs with seed 42.
Data augmentation includes additive Gaussian noise on the mean-action vector ($\sigma \in [0.02, 0.1]$) and uncertainty features ($\sigma \approx 0.006$).
The default magnitude bound is $\varepsilon = 0.2$ for all CRM variants unless stated otherwise.

\paragraph{Statistical protocol.}
Table~\ref{tab:main} reports seed 42 (10 rollouts $\times$ 10 tasks = 100 episodes per suite).
For the primary comparison, we replicate across multiple seeds on LIBERO-Object: obs\_only ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$, 6 seeds) achieves mean $17.5 \pm 2.8$\%, VLA-only (5 seeds) achieves mean $11.2 \pm 1.6$\%, and Argmin (5 seeds) achieves mean $12.4 \pm 2.9$\%.
Pooled Fisher's exact test: obs\_only vs.\ VLA-only yields $p = 0.0074$ (Cohen's $d = 1.21$).
All six obs\_only seeds exceed the VLA-only mean, confirming reproducible improvement despite per-seed variance.
Multi-seed VLA-mean evaluation (4 seeds, mean 12.5\%) confirms that averaging provides no consistent benefit over single-sample execution.


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main_results}

Table~\ref{tab:main} compares all methods on both benchmarks.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Task success rate (\%\,$\uparrow$) on LIBERO-Object and LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks $\times$ 10 rollouts each, seed 42). $\Delta$ denotes improvement over the Argmin selection baseline. All methods use the same frozen SmolVLA checkpoint.}
\label{tab:main}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
Method & Object (\%) & Spatial (\%) & $\Delta$ Object \\
\midrule
VLA-only ($K{=}1$)    & 12.0 & 30.0 & $\phantom{+}0.0$ \\
VLA-mean ($K{=}10$)   & 12.0 & 32.0 & $\phantom{+}0.0$ \\
Argmin ($K{=}10$)      & 12.0 & 34.0 & --- \\
\midrule
scalar ($\varepsilon{=}0.1$)  & \phantom{0}9.0 & 32.0 & $-3.0$ \\
perdof ($\varepsilon{=}0.1$)  & 11.0 & 35.0 & $-1.0$ \\
\textbf{obs\_only} ($\varepsilon{=}0.1$) & \textbf{19.0} & \textbf{35.0} & $\mathbf{+7.0}$ \\
\midrule
obs\_only ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$) & \textbf{22.0} & 35.0 & $+10.0$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Object benchmark: correction helps.}
On LIBERO-Object, obs\_only at $\varepsilon{=}0.1$ achieves 19.0\% (seed 42), and at $\varepsilon{=}0.2$ yields 22.0\%.
Across six seeds ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$), the pipeline achieves mean $17.5 \pm 2.8$\% versus VLA-only mean $11.2 \pm 1.6$\% ($p = 0.0074$, pooled Fisher's exact test; Cohen's $d = 1.21$).
The improvement over Argmin (mean $12.4 \pm 2.9$\%) is +5.1\,pp.

At seed 42, three baselines (VLA-only, VLA-mean, and Argmin) all achieve 12.0\%, indicating that neither multi-sample averaging nor $L_2$ argmin selection provides meaningful benefit on this task suite.
The VLA-mean result is informative: averaging 10 independent flow-matching samples does not reduce error compared to a single sample ($K{=}1$), confirming that action diversity does not center around the correct action.
The obs\_only CRM breaks through this plateau by predicting corrective residuals conditioned on the observation embedding.

\paragraph{Pipeline decomposition: selection and correction are synergistic.}
To isolate contributions, we evaluate the CRM without multi-sample selection ($K{=}1$): the CRM corrects a single VLA output directly.
At $K{=}1$, CRM correction achieves 10.3\% (3-seed mean), at the VLA-only level (11.2\%).
Argmin selection without correction achieves 12.4\% (5-seed mean), a modest +1.2\,pp gain.
Neither component alone meaningfully improves the frozen VLA, yet the full pipeline ($K{=}10$, selection + correction) achieves 17.5\%, a +6.3\,pp gain ($p = 0.0074$).
This synergy arises because argmin selection filters out the worst samples, providing the CRM with a higher-quality starting point; the CRM then applies corrections that are more reliable on these pre-screened candidates.
In terms of contribution decomposition: selection accounts for ${\sim}$1\,pp and correction for ${\sim}$5\,pp, with correction 4--5$\times$ more valuable than selection alone.

\paragraph{Spatial benchmark: correction does not help.}
On LIBERO-Spatial, all methods cluster within a 5\,pp band (30--35\%).
The best CRM variants (obs\_only, perdof) achieve 35\%, only 1\,pp above the Argmin baseline (34\%).
This is a null result that we report prominently.

We interpret this as follows: spatial perturbations in LIBERO-Spatial involve changes to object layout (e.g., moving target locations), which may require re-planning rather than local action correction.
The VLA's observation encoder cannot extract correctable error signals from spatial shifts. The problem is not that actions are inaccurate given the current state, but that the task structure itself has changed.
Residual correction at the action level is the wrong granularity for this type of generalization.

\paragraph{Key finding.}
The full pipeline significantly improves over VLA-only for object manipulation ($p < 0.01$), where the challenge is fine-grained motor control with novel objects.
For spatial reasoning, where the challenge is planning under layout changes, correction at the action level provides no benefit over selection alone.


\subsection{CRM Conditioning Ablation}
\label{sec:ablation}

We focus the conditioning ablation on LIBERO-Object, where meaningful differences emerge (Table~\ref{tab:main}).

\paragraph{Ranking.}
obs\_only (19.0\%) $\gg$ Argmin (12.0\%) $\approx$ perdof (11.0\%) $>$ scalar (9.0\%).

This ordering is the central negative result of our ablation: per-DOF conformal features, despite being intuitively richer (40 additional dimensions capturing per-DOF standard deviations, conformal radii, and log-volume terms), \emph{hurt} rather than help.
Scalar uncertainty conditioning (1 additional dimension) performs even worse, falling 3.0\,pp below the Argmin baseline that uses no correction at all.

The scalar $<$ perdof ordering is consistent across seeds (scalar: 9\%/6\% for seeds 42/44; perdof: 11\%/8\%).
One-dimensional scalar uncertainty compresses all six action dimensions into a single number.
When certain dimensions carry high uncertainty but the correction direction is already correct along those axes, the scalar signal cannot distinguish this case from one where correction is needed everywhere.
The result is uniform over-correction or under-correction across all dimensions.
Per-DOF conditioning at least permits dimension-specific judgments, though at $K{=}10$ these judgments remain too noisy to be useful.
Even 1D scalar uncertainty conditioning is harmful, confirming that conformal scores at $K{=}10$ are unreliable regardless of aggregation dimensionality.
The noise originates in the score itself (rank-deficient covariance estimate from 10 samples in 6D), not in how these scores are decomposed across dimensions.

\paragraph{Why does richer conditioning fail?}
We identify three factors:

\emph{(1) Noisy covariance estimation.}
With $K{=}10$ samples in $d{=}6$ dimensions, the dimension-to-sample ratio is $d/K = 0.6$.
While Ledoit--Wolf shrinkage~\cite{ledoit2004well} stabilizes the covariance estimate for selection (Section~\ref{sec:selection}), the per-DOF features derived from this estimate (standard deviations, conformal radii) still carry substantial estimation noise.
Feeding these noisy features as CRM input introduces a distribution shift between training data (where noise patterns are consistent) and closed-loop evaluation (where compounding state-distribution drift produces different noise patterns).

\emph{(2) Observation features are sufficient.}
The frozen VLA observation embedding $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}} \in \mathbb{R}^{960}$ already encodes task-relevant geometric information: object identity, spatial layout, gripper-object relationship, and task progress.
This information subsumes what the per-DOF conformal features attempt to capture, namely which action dimensions are uncertain given the current scene.
The CRM learns to map directly from scene understanding to corrective residuals, without the intermediate conformal statistics.

\emph{(3) Per-step MSE $\neq$ episode success.}
All CRM variants achieve low per-step MSE on held-out demonstration data, yet offline prediction accuracy does not predict closed-loop task success.
In closed-loop evaluation, small per-step errors compound and the robot visits states far from the demonstration distribution~\cite{ross2011dagger}.
The noisy conformal features amplify this drift: occasional erroneous correction directions, even when small in magnitude, can trigger cascading failures in individual episodes.

\paragraph{Connection to magnitude sensitivity.}
The obs\_only variant is also more robust across magnitude bounds $\varepsilon$ than perdof (Section~\ref{sec:magnitude_results}), providing further evidence that observation-only conditioning yields a more stable correction signal.


\subsection{Conditioning-Magnitude Interaction}
\label{sec:magnitude_results}

The norm bound $\varepsilon$ controls how far the CRM can deviate from the selected action.
Figure~\ref{fig:magnitude} plots success rate against $\varepsilon$ on LIBERO-Object for both conditioning variants.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/fig2_magnitude.pdf}
\caption{Success rate (\%) vs.\ magnitude bound $\varepsilon$ on LIBERO-Object. obs\_only (blue) remains above the VLA-only baseline (11.2\%, dashed) across all tested $\varepsilon$ including uncapped (${\approx}$1.42). perdof (orange) collapses progressively, reaching 0\% at the uncapped setting (3 seeds). Error bars: $\pm$1 std; hollow markers: $n < 3$.}
\label{fig:magnitude}
\end{figure}

\paragraph{obs\_only is robust across all magnitudes.}
The obs\_only variant maintains 13.5--17.5\% across $\varepsilon \in [0.03, \text{uncapped}]$, peaking at 17.5\% ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$, 6 seeds) and remaining above VLA-only (11.2\%) at every tested bound, including uncapped (14.3\%, 3 seeds).
The practitioner need not carefully tune $\varepsilon$: any value in $[0.05, 0.3]$ yields comparable performance.

\paragraph{perdof collapses progressively.}
The perdof variant starts at 14.0\% ($\varepsilon{=}0.03$, $n{=}1$), drops to 11.0\% at $\varepsilon{=}0.1$ (6 seeds), and collapses to 0\% at the uncapped setting (3 seeds, all zero).
This progressive degradation traces to rank-deficient covariance estimation: with $K{=}10$ samples in $d{=}6$ dimensions ($d/K = 0.6$), per-DOF features carry substantial estimation noise.
At tight $\varepsilon$, clipping masks the noisy correction directions; as the bound loosens, erroneous corrections compound across the trajectory.

\paragraph{Scalar conditioning is worse than no conditioning.}
The scalar variant achieves 8.3\% (3 seeds at $\varepsilon{=}0.2$), below VLA-only (11.2\%).
This confirms that conformal statistics at $K{=}10$ are unreliable regardless of aggregation dimensionality: the noise originates in the score itself (rank-deficient covariance), not in how the scores are decomposed.

\paragraph{Practical recommendation.}
We use $\varepsilon{=}0.2$ as the primary setting.
Within $[0.05, 0.3]$, obs\_only never degrades below the VLA-only baseline across all tested seeds.


\subsection{Inference-Time Scaling with $K$}
\label{sec:k_scaling}

Figure~\ref{fig:kvalue} plots task success rate against the number of VLA samples $K$.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/fig3_kvalue.pdf}
\caption{Success rate (\%) vs.\ number of VLA samples $K$ on LIBERO-Object (obs\_only, $\varepsilon{=}0.2$). Reference lines: VLA-only (11.2\%, 5 seeds) and Argmin-only (12.4\%, 5 seeds). Error bars: $\pm$1 std where available; hollow marker for $K{=}5$ ($n{=}1$).}
\label{fig:kvalue}
\end{figure}

Performance increases monotonically with $K$: $K{=}1$ (10.3\%, 3 seeds) $\to$ $K{=}5$ (14.0\%, 1 seed) $\to$ $K{=}10$ (17.5\%, 6 seeds).
At $K{=}1$, CRM correction alone performs at the VLA-only level (11.2\%), confirming that the correction module requires multi-sample selection to be effective.
The monotonic trend parallels inference-time compute scaling in LLMs~\cite{snell2024scaling}, where repeated sampling with selection (best-of-$N$) improves output quality.
In our setting, more samples yield a better argmin starting point, which in turn enables more effective correction.

The $K{=}5$ data point is preliminary ($n{=}1$), but it falls on the monotonic trend, suggesting that even moderate sample budgets can capture partial gains.
The compute cost scales linearly: $K{=}10$ requires 10 forward passes through the frozen VLA plus ${\sim}$3\,ms for CRM inference, a ${\sim}$10$\times$ increase in VLA compute.


\subsection{Applicability Boundary: Stochastic VLA Diversity}
\label{sec:applicability}

The multi-sample pipeline requires stochastic action diversity across samples. We test this prerequisite by comparing SmolVLA (flow-matching, 450M) with OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024openvla} (autoregressive tokenization, 7B).

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/fig4_diversity.pdf}
\caption{Per-DOF action variance (log scale) across $K{=}10$ samples for SmolVLA (flow-matching) and OpenVLA (tokenized). OpenVLA produces 8/10 identical samples at temperature $T{=}0.5$, with per-DOF variance below $10^{-30}$ for most dimensions.}
\label{fig:diversity}
\end{figure}

Figure~\ref{fig:diversity} shows the contrast: SmolVLA produces meaningfully diverse samples across all action dimensions, while OpenVLA at temperature $T{=}0.5$ generates 8 out of 10 identical action sequences, with per-DOF variance below $10^{-30}$ for most dimensions.
This near-determinism arises from autoregressive token selection: the argmax decoding at each token position collapses the distribution to a single mode, and moderate temperature fails to overcome the peaked distribution.

This result establishes an applicability boundary: multi-sample inference-time correction is specific to stochastic generative VLAs (flow-matching, diffusion). Tokenized VLAs lack the action diversity that selection and correction rely on.
The boundary is architectural, not a limitation of our method: any inference-time approach that draws multiple action candidates requires the base policy to produce diverse samples.


\subsection{Per-Task Analysis}
\label{sec:per_task}

Table~\ref{tab:pertask} reports per-task success rates on LIBERO-Object (seed 42) for the VLA-only baseline, Argmin selection, and obs\_only at two magnitude bounds.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Per-task success rate (\%) on LIBERO-Object (seed 42, 10 rollouts per task). Tasks ordered by obs\_only $\varepsilon{=}0.2$ improvement over VLA-only.}
\label{tab:pertask}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
Task & VLA-only & Argmin & obs\_only 0.1 & obs\_only 0.2 \\
\midrule
chocolate\_pudding & 20 & 30 & 50 & 60 \\
ketchup            &  0 &  0 & 10 & 20 \\
bbq\_sauce         & 20 & 30 & 40 & 40 \\
salad\_dressing    & 20 & 10 & 20 & 30 \\
butter             &  0 & 10 & 10 & 10 \\
milk               & 10 & 10 & 20 & 20 \\
orange\_juice      & 30 & 30 & 30 & 30 \\
tomato\_sauce      & 10 &  0 &  0 & 10 \\
alphabet\_soup     &  0 &  0 &  0 &  0 \\
cream\_cheese      & 10 &  0 & 10 &  0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Improvement concentrates on medium-difficulty tasks.}
The +10\,pp aggregate gain of obs\_only ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$) over VLA-only is not uniformly distributed across tasks.
The largest improvements appear on tasks where the frozen VLA partially succeeds but makes correctable errors: chocolate\_pudding (+40\,pp, from 20\% to 60\%), bbq\_sauce and ketchup (+20\,pp each), and salad\_dressing (+10\,pp).
These four tasks account for 9 of the 10 additional successes.
Conversely, four tasks (alphabet\_soup, cream\_cheese, tomato\_sauce, butter) remain at 0--10\% across all methods, including obs\_only.
For these tasks, the base policy fails so completely that local action-level correction cannot recover a viable trajectory.

\paragraph{Implications for the correction mechanism.}
Correction benefits tasks where the frozen VLA partially succeeds but makes correctable errors, rather than tasks where the base policy fails catastrophically or already succeeds reliably.
This pattern is expected for a residual correction approach bounded by $\varepsilon$: the CRM can fix small deviations in grasp pose or approach angle, but cannot recover from fundamental planning failures (e.g., reaching toward the wrong object entirely).
The concentrated improvement profile also addresses the question of effect size: the aggregate +10\,pp is not a uniform +1\,pp across 10 tasks, but a substantial +20--40\,pp on specific tasks diluted by tasks outside the correctable regime.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

% --- Para 1: VLAs are impressive but fragile under distribution shift ---
Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) that generate actions via flow matching~\cite{black2024pi0,shukor2025smolvla,lipman2023flow} have reached near-saturation on in-distribution benchmarks such as LIBERO~\cite{liu2023libero}.
Yet this performance masks severe fragility: visual and physical perturbations common in deployment (camera viewpoint shifts, object layout changes, robot initial-state variation) routinely degrade success by over 65 percentage points.
On the LIBERO+ benchmark~\cite{fei2025liberoplus}, $\pi_0$ drops from 94.2\% to 6.6\% under initial-state perturbation, and UniVLA drops from 95.2\% to 4.3\% under viewpoint changes.
Closing this robustness gap without retraining the base policy is a prerequisite for deploying VLAs outside tightly controlled laboratory settings.

% --- Para 2: Existing approaches and the gap ---
Two lines of work address this challenge.
Training-time methods improve the base policy through robustness-aware objectives~\cite{srpo2025,robustvla2025,digflow2025} or test-time reinforcement learning~\cite{liu2026ttvla}, but require retraining or per-task RL and remain bounded by the training distribution.
Inference-time methods leave the policy frozen: ReconVLA~\cite{chen2026reconvla} applies conformal quantile regression for uncertainty quantification and out-of-distribution detection, but does not learn corrective residuals; A2C2~\cite{a2c2_2025} trains a per-step correction head on frozen VLA action chunks, but applies correction unconditionally without multi-sample selection or explicit magnitude control; VLA-Pilot~\cite{li2025vlapilot} applies evolutionary optimization over action samples, but incurs 2.41\,s per control step.
Despite growing interest in inference-time action refinement, fundamental design questions remain unanswered: how much does candidate selection contribute relative to learned correction?
What observation features should condition the correction module?
How sensitive is closed-loop performance to correction magnitude?
No existing work provides a systematic decomposition of these factors.

% --- Para 3: Our approach — sample-then-correct ---
We introduce ACR-VLA, an inference-time action refinement module for frozen flow-matching VLAs.
At each control step, ACR-VLA draws $K{=}10$ action samples from the frozen VLA, selects the candidate closest to the sample mean by $L_2$ distance, and applies a learned residual correction via a lightweight Conformal Residual Module (CRM).
The CRM is a ${\sim}$327K-parameter MLP that takes as input the frozen VLA's observation embedding ($\mathbb{R}^{960}$) concatenated with the selected action ($\mathbb{R}^{30}$) and predicts a residual $\boldsymbol{\delta}$ whose $L_2$ norm is clipped to a bound $\varepsilon$, producing the corrected action $\mathbf{a}^* = a_{\mathrm{base}} + \mathrm{clip}(\boldsymbol{\delta})$.
The key design insight is twofold: correction on a pre-screened starting point is more reliable than correction on an arbitrary single sample, and bounding the correction magnitude prevents compounding errors from destabilizing the closed-loop trajectory.
The base VLA is never modified; ACR-VLA attaches as a post-hoc module to any frozen flow-matching VLA.

% --- Para 4: Three key findings ---
We evaluate ACR-VLA on LIBERO-Object and LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks, 100 trials each) using SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} as the frozen backbone.
Three findings emerge.

\textbf{(1) The full pipeline significantly improves over the frozen VLA, with correction as the dominant factor.}
With observation-only conditioning at $\varepsilon{=}0.2$, the pipeline achieves 17.5\% mean success across 6 seeds versus 11.2\% for VLA-only across 5 seeds (+6.3\,pp, pooled Fisher's exact $p = 0.0074$, Cohen's $d = 1.21$).
Component decomposition reveals that correction accounts for ${\sim}$5\,pp and selection for ${\sim}$1\,pp: at $K{=}1$ (correction without selection), success is 10.3\%, at the VLA-only level; argmin selection alone yields 12.4\%.
Neither component suffices in isolation.
On LIBERO-Spatial, all methods cluster within 30--35\%, a null result that bounds the scope of action-level correction to object-centric manipulation (Section~\ref{sec:main_results}, Table~\ref{tab:main}).

\textbf{(2) Observation features suffice for correction; conformal uncertainty features hurt.}
We compare three CRM conditioning variants at fixed $\varepsilon{=}0.1$: observation-only conditioning (19\%, seed 42) substantially outperforms per-DOF conformal conditioning (11\%), argmin selection alone (12\%), and scalar uncertainty conditioning (9\%).
The observation-only variant is also robust across magnitude bounds, maintaining 13.5--17.5\% for all tested $\varepsilon$, while per-DOF conditioning collapses from 14\% to 0\% as $\varepsilon$ increases.
The root cause is rank-deficient covariance estimation at $K{=}10$ samples in 6 dimensions (Section~\ref{sec:ablation}, Section~\ref{sec:magnitude_results}).

\textbf{(3) Multi-sample correction requires stochastic action diversity.}
SmolVLA (flow-matching) produces diverse samples suitable for selection and correction.
OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024openvla} (autoregressive tokenization) generates 8 out of 10 identical samples with per-DOF variance below $10^{-30}$.
This establishes an architectural applicability boundary: the pipeline is specific to stochastic generative VLAs (Section~\ref{sec:applicability}, Figure~\ref{fig:diversity}).

% --- Para 5: Contributions ---
Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{A multi-sample inference-time correction pipeline with component decomposition.}
  We propose ACR-VLA, which combines $L_2$ argmin selection with bounded residual correction for frozen flow-matching VLAs, and decompose the pipeline into selection (${\sim}$1\,pp) and correction (${\sim}$5\,pp) contributions.
  The full pipeline achieves a statistically significant +6.3\,pp improvement over the frozen VLA baseline ($p = 0.0074$, 6 seeds) on LIBERO-Object (Section~\ref{sec:main_results}).

  \item \textbf{First systematic conditioning and magnitude study, with an honest negative on conformal features.}
  We compare three conditioning variants across a $6{\times}$ range of magnitude bounds and find that observation-only conditioning is robust across all settings, while per-DOF conformal features and scalar uncertainty are harmful.
  This challenges the intuition that richer uncertainty features improve correction (Section~\ref{sec:ablation}, Section~\ref{sec:magnitude_results}).

  \item \textbf{Applicability boundary: stochastic diversity as a prerequisite.}
  We show that tokenized VLAs lack the sample diversity required for multi-sample correction and that action-level correction does not transfer to spatial reasoning tasks, establishing clear scope boundaries for inference-time action refinement (Section~\ref{sec:applicability}).
\end{enumerate}
